bio:
Hello, 안녕하세요! I'm Hana, an M.S. student in Intelligence and Information at Seoul National University, advised by Professor Bongwon Suh. My research focuses on the intersection of human-AI interaction and artificial intelligence.

Human experiences are incredibly diverse, requiring a range of approaches to understand them. While many AI systems capture experience through multimodal inputs such as images and audio, I believe we also need complementary ways to understand individual intent and values. My work explores a more person-centered direction—starting from what people explicitly express, including their thoughts, everyday conversations, and journal entries.

As these personal archives accumulate, a key challenge is how AI agents can organize and decompose them, preserve their original context, and derive meaningful abstractions. I study memory representations and computational methods for managing this process while keeping abstractions grounded in the source material and a person's perspective. My work combines technical development of these methods with interactive systems and user-centered evaluation. Ultimately, I aim to contribute to the evolution of AI from general-purpose tools into truly collaborative, personalized agents.

Before my master's, I earned a B.S. in Computer Science and Engineering with a double major in Business Administration from Seoul National University. As an undergraduate, I researched deepfake awareness among older adults and published a CHI '26 paper under the mentorship of Professor Hajin Lim. I also expanded my research experience during a summer internship at KAIST, guided by Professor Juho Kim.

outside:
Alongside that work, I have been building a small world building project: one place to keep the words, images, sites, people, and traces that matter to me beyond research.

I use it to collect things that do not fit neatly into academic categories, but still shape how I think and what I want to keep learning from.

Right now it includes a small Daemari translation archive, SHANUM community work, and references I keep returning to, alongside my interest in speculative thought and speculative ways of thinking.

I also like playing tennis and drawing, especially watercolor and small doodles, and I keep a drawing journal when I travel or visit new places.
